title: Jiujiang
capsule: The Kingdom of Jiujiang was granted by Xiang Yu in 206 BC to Ying Bu, a Chu general who had served under him, comprising territory in modern central and southern Anhui along the lower Yangzi. As one of the more militarily capable of the Eighteen Kingdoms' rulers, Ying Bu was implicated in the assassination of the figurehead Emperor Yi of Chu on Xiang Yu's secret orders, an act that helped delegitimize Xiang Yu's settlement. Ying Bu later defected to Liu Bang during the Chu–Han Contention, and Jiujiang's territory was absorbed into the expanding Han domain after the Eighteen Kingdoms' collapse by 203 BC.
